newsitem.title: USA: America Online Inc raises bar for vendors.
newsitem.headline: America Online Inc raises bar for vendors.

text.p: America Online Inc (AOL), the online provider with the largest subscriber pool, has raised the bar for many of the eletronic retailers doing business via its service.

Starting next month, retailers that used to pay commissions to AOL for the right to peddle their wares on its Market Place service will pay a flat fee. AOL hopes the plan will attract a new class of vendors and provide a more efficient shopping service to subscribers.

"We have the most valuable real estate in cyberspace," said Wendy Goldberg, a spokesperson for AOL on Monday. "We want to encourage our merchandise partners to value their online real estate with the same seriousness as if they were in a real mall," she added.
The plan also carries financial benefits for AOL, analysts said.
"I think it's a good idea for them.... AOL is starting to realize the value of its own real estate," said Patrick Keane, an analyst with Jupiter Communications.

Keane said he didn't look at the move as an admission that the commission fee system was unsuccessful. Rather, he said, "it points to the fact that AOL has to do anything it can to diversify revenues."

Keane said that the company, which currently earns about 85 percent of its revenues from access fees, would likely achieve a more balanced revenue sheet under the new plan, but that smaller retailers, unable to pay the flat fees, might fall away.

Until now, Goldberg said, most of the company's electronic retailers paid commissions of about 10 percent to 20 percent of their sales in exchange for an online storefront on AOL's Market Place. However, charging commissions does not provide an incentive to generate sales and online merchants need not fret over meeting expectations if they choose to look on their electronic storefronts as experiments.
When AOL replaces Market Place with its new Shopping Channel in late August, retailers appearing there will pay a flat fee, starting at $125,000, for a year's lease.

Companies deciding to pay "rent" on the Shopping Channel will have a larger stake in their online business and will be more likely to put their best foot forward in terms of advertising and presentation, Goldberg said.
AOL has already signed agreements with book seller Barnes & Noble Inc and 1-800 Flowers to set up shop in its new online mall.
